name: init_module
synopsis: int syscall(SYS_init_module, void *module_image, unsigned long len, const char *param_values);
int syscall(SYS_finit_module, int fd, const char *param_values, int flags);
description: The init_module system call loads an ELF image into kernel space, initializes module parameters, and runs the module's init function, requiring appropriate privileges. The finit_module system call performs a similar operation but reads the module from a file descriptor, potentially avoiding signature verification overhead.

parameters.name: module_image
parameters.description: Pointer to a buffer containing the binary ELF image to be loaded

parameters.name: param_values
parameters.description: String containing space-delimited specifications for module parameters

parameters.name: fd
parameters.description: File descriptor from which to read the module

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Bit mask flags for finit_module, such as MODULE_INIT_IGNORE_MODVERSIONS

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, errno is set

errors.description: Timeout while trying to resolve a symbol reference
An address argument referred to an invalid location
Module signature is invalid or no key available (only if CONFIG_MODULE_SIG_FORCE is enabled)
Caller lacks CAP_SYS_MODULE capability or module loading is disabled
A module with this name is already loaded (init_module only)
Invalid param_values, ELF image inconsistencies, or invalid flags
The binary image is not a valid ELF image or for a different architecture
File descriptor is not open for reading (finit_module only)
File referred to by fd is too large (finit_module only)
File referred to by fd is open for read-write (finit_module only)

versions: Linux 2.6 for init_module; Linux 3.8 for finit_module
